definitions.explanation: The act of reworking or adapting an existing creative work — a novel, play, film, or other piece — into a new version. This often involves changing the medium, updating the setting, or altering the story to suit a different audience.

examples.japanese: {小説|しょうせつ}を{改作|かいさく}した。
{原作|げんさく}を{舞台|ぶたい}{用|よう}に{改作|かいさく}する{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: They plan to adapt the original work for the stage.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{戯曲|ぎきょく}を{改作|かいさく}したもので、{現代|げんだい}の{観客|かんきゃく}にも{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: This film is an adaptation of a famous play and is popular with modern audiences as well.

notes:
Composed of {改|かい} (reform, change) and {作|さく} (work, production). Refers specifically to reworking an existing creative work rather than creating something from scratch. Most commonly used in literary, theatrical, and film contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小説|しょうせつ}の{改作|かいさく}: adaptation of a novel
- {舞台|ぶたい}{用|よう}に{改作|かいさく}する: to adapt for the stage
- {改作|かいさく}{版|ばん}: adapted version
- {原作|げんさく}を{改作|かいさく}する: to adapt an original work

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {翻案|ほんあん}: adaptation — emphasizes creative reinterpretation, often freer than {改作|かいさく}
- {脚色|きゃくしょく}: dramatization — specifically adapting for stage or screen
- {改編|かいへん}: reorganization; adaptation — broader, can apply to organizational restructuring as well as creative works
